source_ref: Mendeley Data 10.17632/95cmh2ftwk, BICDIS.sav (sha256 3b6d80f9a158e9f19c41d6a6aa8c6e6c76781158bf4c770421bcb92de9195581), variable labels + value labels of DASS1..DASS21; paper PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0276027 checked (no item text)
note: Item codes DASS1..DASS21 ARE the source column names in the deposit's BICDIS.sav (Mendeley 10.17632/95cmh2ftwk, CC BY 4.0), which data/doherty_2023_bicdis.py melts unchanged; item_text is each column's SPSS variable label and option_text is its value labels (identical value-label set on all 21 columns), both read directly with pyreadstat. Cross-check: the labels run in canonical DASS-21 order, and summing the canonical subscale sets (stress 1,6,8,11,12,14,18; anxiety 2,4,7,9,15,19,20; depression 3,5,10,13,16,17,21) reproduces the deposit's own DASSsubscaleSt/Anx/Dep columns exactly on 414/420/414 of 414/420/414 complete cases and the paper's Table 2 (stress 6.0 (4.4), anxiety 1.6 (2.5), depression 3.3 (4.0)); per-item n and mean of the .sav equal the live table on all 21 items. Deviations from the literal labels, all cosmetic: lowercase 'i' capitalised in DASS2 and DASS19; 'meaninglesss' -> 'meaningless' in DASS21; a non-breaking space + space collapsed to one space in DASS17. The resp=2 value label is truncated in the .sav at 60 characters ('Applied to me to a considerable degree, ora good part of tim'); shipped as 'Applied to me to a considerable degree, or a good part of time', the completion taken from the canonical DASS anchor ('...considerable degree or a good part of time'), keeping the study's comma. Labels that differ from the canonical DASS-21 wording were NOT normalised and are shipped as the deposit states them: resp=1 reads 'Applied to me to some degree, or a good part of time' (canonical: 'or some of the time'); DASS4 lacks 'breathlessness' (canonical: 'excessively rapid breathing, breathlessness in the absence of physical exertion'); DASS9 reads 'I worried about' (canonical: 'I was worried about'). Whether these are the administered online wording or the labeller's shorthand is not recoverable: the paper (PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0276027) names the DASS and describes a 4-point scale but prints no items, anchors or instructions and has no questionnaire supplement. instructions left blank: neither the deposit nor the paper states them, and the canonical paper-form DASS instruction ('circle a number 0, 1, 2 or 3 ... over the past week') was not imported for an online survey. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv verdict 'ship' for DASS applied (UNSW DASS FAQ, http://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/DASSFAQ.htm: 'The DASS questionnaire is public domain, and so permission is not needed to use it.'); English original, so no translation question.
public_note: Item and option wording is the deposit's SPSS labels, which differ from the canonical DASS-21 in three places that were kept as found: the resp=1 anchor reads 'or a good part of time' (canonical 'or some of the time', making it nearly identical to the resp=2 anchor), item DASS4 omits 'breathlessness', and DASS9 reads 'I worried' for 'I was worried'

Cross-check: S1 File .xlsx, .s001 (sha256 53f9606d88a887a1871417c8d5c0597bbc88ad8634b68bc9d31e5a15aeff58c1), headers '1.Intention'..'6.Intention'. Paper Table 1 image .t001 (sha256 5c4e8e84816e72f408e1a9cbccef16b5c05f055b1878fd4087b279213368fa06). Instrument: Ozkurt B (2023) doctoral dissertation, Sakarya Uygulamali Bilimler Universitesi. Checked and NOT the administered wording: Ozkurt B, Altin Y, Eskiler E, Kucukibis HF (2025) Spormetre 23(2):26-48, doi:10.33689/spormetre.1593920, PDF https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/4405625 (sha256 8e97ae801bec449676fbefd1b0ce3b2bb1e68124d0d171e5af5b35f36bf2d77c, fetched 2026-09-25). Processing script data/ozkurt_2026_wrestlers.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/ozkurt_2026_continuance_intention/.
note: Code axis: IRW item codes ARE the .sav column names (data/ozkurt_2026_wrestlers.py melts r'INT\d+$', renames nothing); .sav labels are position-numbered only, so wording comes from S6 Table 6 against 'Original item no.' -> paper_explicit. Wording is S6's English verbatim; administered in Turkish, no Turkish wording in the article or any supplement (S1 headers, S2 labels, S6, S7 codebook all English) -> translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied, language=Turkish. No instructions published; scale points 2-6 unlabelled and left blank. OVERRIDE OF STATED CODING (INT2, INT3): S6 marks items 2-3 'reverse-coded in original form' and states 1=Strongly Disagree..7=Strongly Agree, but the data store them ALREADY REVERSED: both correlate +0.34 with INT1 ('I will continue this sport...'), r(INT2,INT3)=0.80, and stored means 4.92/5.24 vs INT1 6.27 (raw reading would have the median elite wrestler agreeing 'I intend to quit'). Their anchors are therefore shipped as 1=Strongly Agree, 7=Strongly Disagree. VERIFICATION (verify_ozkurt_2026_continuance_intention.R, VERDICT: PASS): live counts = .sav counts 6/6; S1 'k.Intention' headers match INT<k> uniquely 6/6; of all 15 four-item subsets only {INT1,INT4,INT5,INT6} (S6's retained 1,4,5,6) reproduces paper Table 1's Intention row: alpha .60 vs .62, r with Enjoyment/Motivation/Competence/Autonomy/Relatedness/Task/Ego .30/.43/.32/.28/.22/.18/.18 vs published .30/.43/.32/.28/.22/.18/.18 (sum|diff| .025; next best .510). RIGHTS: ships. The administered instrument is Ozkurt's own 2023 dissertation form; its English wording is published by the same author under CC BY 4.0 in S6. The later Spormetre 2025 scale that the paper cites as the validation is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 ('licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-Non-Derivatives 4.0 International Licence', PDF sha256 8e97ae80...) but is a DIFFERENT six-item, 5-point, all-positive scale (EK 1: 'Bu spora devam etmeye kararliyim.' ...); none of the six S6 items appears in it, so that licence does not reach this wording. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows).
public_note: Items INT2 ('I often think about quitting this sport.') and INT3 ('I intend to quit this sport.') are stored reverse-scored in the response data (they correlate +0.34 with INT1, 'I will continue this sport'), so for these two items resp 7 means strong DISAGREEMENT with the printed wording; the English is the study's own rendering of a Turkish administration.

note: mapping_basis=data_labels: data/zeng_2025_megaproject.py names each item item_4_N from the '4.N' number inside the S1 column header (number-preserving rename, regex (\d+)\.(\d+); for 4.1 it skips the banner's '4. ' because no digit follows), and that header carries the full bilingual wording, so code and text are tied at the source (15/15). Live table matches S1: n=458 per item, means identical (e.g. item_4_1 3.45, item_4_12 3.60). Bilingual form (S2: 'This questionnaire is divided into two languages, Chinese and English, please read according to your own situation'), so language='Chinese; English', base fields Chinese, _translated the form's own English, split at the first Latin letter; leading '4.N' numbering stripped; banner title line moved to instrument; otherwise verbatim. CAVEATS: the paper's SECM is 8 items (= item_4_8..item_4_15; S2 numbers them 4.1-4.8, paper SECM1-8); item_4_1..item_4_7 (pollution types) are in S1 only, their anchors inferred from their being rows of the same section-4 matrix (single banner on 4.1; cross-block r +0.64..+0.75), and their sub-header, if any, is unpublished. S2's row header 'Your satisfaction level of current environmental compensation measures' shipped as section_prompt for item_4_8..4_15 only. Direction: paper states 1 ('not satisfied at all') to 5 ('very satisfied'); S2 prints anchors left to right in that order; S1 stores integers 1-5. Rights: the study's own scale ('This study developed an eight-item scale', adapting an MNRE method and Li and Ng [64]); project-specific wording under the article's CC BY 4.0; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located; no register row matches (silence, not a grant; no register row written). validate_items.R --table-sets: item and resp sets PASS (15 items, resp 1-5).
public_note: Item codes follow the data file's numbering, not the questionnaire's: item_4_8 to item_4_15 are the paper's eight-item SECM scale (SECM1-SECM8), while item_4_1 to item_4_7 are pollution-type items that appear in the data file but not in the published questionnaire, so their response labels are inferred from the shared matrix and any lead-in prompt they had is unknown
